name: addEventListener()
description: Registers a function to be called whenever the specified event fires on the target.
parameters: type — event name, e.g. 'click'. listener — the callback function. options — optional object with capture, once, passive, signal.
notes: Multiple listeners can be attached to the same event without overwriting each other, unlike onclick assignment.

name: removeEventListener()
description: Unregisters an event listener previously added with addEventListener().
parameters: type — event name. listener — reference to the exact function passed to addEventListener(). options — must match capture value used when adding.
notes: Anonymous/inline arrow functions can't be removed since removeEventListener() needs a reference to the same function instance.

name: Event object properties
description: The event object passed to a listener carries details about what happened, such as target (element the event originated on), currentTarget (element the listener is attached to), type, and timeStamp.
notes: target and currentTarget can differ when an event bubbles up from a descendant to an ancestor listener.

name: Event bubbling vs capturing
description: Events travel in three phases: capturing (from window down to the target), target, then bubbling (from the target back up to window). addEventListener() listens on the bubbling phase by default.
example: parent.addEventListener('click', handler, { capture: true }); // fires during capture phase
notes: Pass { capture: true } as the third argument to listen during the capture phase instead of bubbling.

name: Event delegation
description: A pattern where a single listener is attached to a common ancestor instead of many descendants, using event.target to determine which descendant triggered it.
notes: Reduces memory usage and automatically handles dynamically added children that never had their own listener attached.

name: preventDefault()
description: Cancels the browser's default action for an event, such as following a link or submitting a form.
notes: Only works if the event's cancelable property is true; does not stop the event from propagating to other listeners.

name: stopPropagation()
description: Stops an event from continuing to propagate to ancestor (or descendant) elements in the capturing/bubbling chain.
notes: stopImmediatePropagation() additionally prevents other listeners registered on the same element for the same event from running.

name: once / passive options
syntax: target.addEventListener(type, listener, { once: true, passive: true })
description: Options passed to addEventListener(): once automatically removes the listener after it fires a single time; passive tells the browser the listener won't call preventDefault(), allowing smoother scroll performance.
notes: Use passive: true on scroll/touch listeners to avoid blocking the browser's compositor thread.

name: CustomEvent
description: Creates a custom, application-defined event that can carry arbitrary data and be dispatched on any DOM element.
parameters: type — event name. detail — any data to attach. bubbles/cancelable — booleans controlling propagation behavior.
example: el.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('item-added', { detail: { id: 1 }, bubbles: true }));
notes: Listen for it like any built-in event with addEventListener('item-added', handler); data is read from event.detail.

name: dispatchEvent()
description: Synchronously triggers an event on a target, invoking all matching listeners, most commonly used with CustomEvent.
parameters: event — an Event or CustomEvent instance.
returns: false if any listener called preventDefault(), true otherwise.
